n0001.title: GPT-3 And The Scaling Hypothesis
n0001.gist: GPT-3's emergent meta-learning from pure scale-up vindicates the scaling hypothesis that simple neural networks, trained large enough, are the route to general intelligence, a claim experts keep dismissing despite being repeatedly proven right.

n0002.title: Introducing GPT-3
n0002.gist: GPT-3's huge scale-up produced meta-learning and human-like text abilities its predecessor lacked, hinting scaling itself is the secret ingredient.

n0003.title: GPT-3 Abstract
n0003.gist: GPT-3 shows that scaling the same architecture yields unexpected meta-learning, supporting the scaling hypothesis.

n0006.title: Meta-Learning
n0006.gist: GPT-3 quietly demonstrates learning-to-learn, solving diverse tasks from prompts alone without finetuning.

n0009.title: Flexing GPT
n0009.gist: Despite being a small, crude, outdated architecture, GPT-3's outputs and few-shot meta-learning already outpace what standard benchmarks capture.

n0014.title: Baking The Cake
n0014.gist: GPT-3 isn't full AGI but is a genuine advance from unsupervised pretraining, and its scaling curves show no sign of bending despite complaints about cost.

n0022.title: Scaling Laws And Hypothesis
n0022.gist: Empirical scaling laws show GPT-3's loss keeps falling smoothly with size, grounding the radical hypothesis that intelligence itself is just scaled-up simple learning.

n0023.title: Scaling
n0023.gist: GPT-3's loss keeps falling along the same power-law curves as smaller models, with room left before returns diminish.

n0032.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0032.gist: Across many domains, bigger models on harder tasks become more stable, general, and meta-learning-capable, likely because scale forces an ensemble of sub-models toward simple, generalizing solutions.

n0045.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0045.gist: The strong scaling hypothesis holds that one scalable architecture, trained ever larger, will spontaneously grow sophisticated behavior, a claim the author once doubted but now accepts.

n0049.title: Why Does Pretraining Work?
n0049.gist: The pretraining thesis argues that minimizing prediction loss on human text forces a model to acquire real reasoning, though whether this guarantees intelligence in practice remains only partly proven.

n0050.title: The Pretraining Thesis
n0050.gist: Because human text encodes causality, logic, and world knowledge, a model predicting it well must implicitly learn to reason.

n0055.title: From Letters To Sentences
n0055.gist: Training climbs from letter frequencies to spelling to word associations to coherent sentences, each stage squeezing out ever smaller loss gains.

n0064.title: The Last Bits Are Deepest
n0064.gist: The remaining gap to human-level prediction is small in bits but consists entirely of the hardest cases, making the last bits the most cognitively demanding.

n0073.title: Reasons For Doubt
n0073.gist: The pretraining thesis is logically neat but unproven in practice, since many theoretically universal algorithms fail to work at feasible scale.

n0078.title: Open Questions
n0078.gist: No one predicted GPT-3's specific gains in advance, and no one can yet say what a further-scaled successor would learn.

n0085.title: Prospects
n0085.gist: Whether a scaling arms race follows depends less on available hardware than on which organizations have the conviction to bet on the scaling hypothesis, and so far only OpenAI has fully committed.

n0086.title: Secrets And Conviction
n0086.gist: History suggests that knowing a hard problem is solvable, plus conviction to apply existing methods at scale, is often the missing ingredient for progress.

n0091.title: Hardware Overhang
n0091.gist: Google Brain and DeepMind have the hardware and talent to build a GPT-4-scale model but lack belief in the scaling hypothesis, pursuing narrower strategies instead.

n0096.title: OpenAI's Bet
n0096.gist: Lacking Google's resources, OpenAI restructured to fund a startup-like wager on scaling, while rivals remain skeptical and none has yet matched GPT-3.

n0101.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0101.gist: A decade of AI experts confidently dismissed scaling and were repeatedly wrong, speaking in a reassuring 'voice of authority' calibrated to sound the same whether right or wrong.

n0102.title: Keeping Track
n0102.gist: A decade ago almost no one predicted deep learning's rise to 175-billion-parameter models except a few scaling advocates like Moravec who foresaw it from hardware trends.

n0108.title: Just X
n0108.gist: Critics habitually dismiss neural nets as 'just' simple mechanisms, but genuine AI success must look exactly like reducing intelligence to well-defined mechanism, as insiders found when scaling kept working past every expected wall.

n0114.title: The Voice Of Authority
n0114.gist: Respected experts confidently predicted AI limits for years and were wrong, because their reassuring tone is calibrated to sound the same whether or not it proves correct.

n0120.title: Appendix
n0120.gist: Agency is not confined to obviously agentic training data but a useful, convergent capability that large predictive models may acquire from almost any rich enough data.

n0121.title: It From Byte
n0121.gist: Because GPT-3 imitates human-generated agentic text, it inevitably learns to roleplay agents, a capability that generalizes to real actions once given effectors.

n0130.title: All Is Atoms & Void
n0130.gist: Since agency is built from non-agentic physical parts, no data is intrinsically free of the potential to encode it, though ordinary physics data seems unlikely to do so.

n0134.title: Intentional Interpretive Stance
n0134.gist: Treating even non-agentic systems—rivers, Turing machines—as goal-seeking agents is often the simplest, most predictive framing, exactly the kind of efficient shortcut a neural network is likely to learn.

n0161.title: Ambient Agency
n0161.gist: Because agency is a useful convergent capability like Turing-completeness, it is very hard to guarantee that any sufficiently powerful model will remain free of it.
